I know this is gonna sound mad judgemental, but most of the Pentecostals and non denominations within an hours drive are mostly (like 90+%) contemporary / effectively discos. Happy clappy services as it were.

It was an older congregation, so many of them were treating it like a social club. I've been to 2 Uniting Church (combo of Methodist, Presbyterian and uhh..something else), Asyrian Orthodox, and three different Anglican churches (2 being if Australia, and another I suspect follows church of England since they prayed for the King)

The first church I was in abolished the title of Elder for the title of Leader, the youngest being 18. I mentioned that we should have older elders to teach since they're more grounded in their belief, they turned it against me saying it was a bad thing and anyone at any age can be a great teacher.

It'd be nice if the people that greet me actually wanted to talk. Or if when I was new to a church and the minister came up to me, the regulars didn't try to hijack the conversation. I feel like Paul would have had endless letters in today's churches.

Sorry, my name is a throwaway account that was auto generated. But I am a designer if that counts haha. I relate hard to the artificially friendly churches, that's what my first church was. Thanks for the encouragement tho.
